card: This PR modifies wallet fee bumping to prevent replacement transactions from having an nLockTime older than the transaction being replaced. Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping feature randomly backdates transaction locktimes by up to 99 blocks about 10% of the time, which during bumpfee can set a locktime earlier than the original transaction. This anomaly serves as an on-chain fingerprint identifying Bitcoin Core and Electrum wallets. Empirical analysis cited in the PR found roughly 200 to 300 such backdated replacements per week across over one million surveyed RBF transactions.
changed_since_previous: No substantial behavioral changes; contains minor test adjustments and cleanups.
evidence: Author's empirical transaction analysis: 'In total we have over 1,000,000 rbf transactions, but we see that on average there are only about 200-300 hundred replaccements backdating per week... less than 2% of all the transactions that have been replaced. However, the few transactions that do exhibit backdating are easily fingerprintable as having been replaced using bumpfee in Bitcoin Core or Electrum.'
problem: Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping logic randomly backdates transaction locktimes by up to 99 blocks approximately 10% of the time. When bumping fees, this random backdating can cause a replacement transaction to have an earlier locktime than the original, creating an unnatural on-chain pattern that acts as a fingerprint identifying Bitcoin Core or Electrum wallets.

risk.why: A flaw in replacement locktime calculations or bounds checks could produce transactions that fail standardness or mempool validation, preventing users from bumping transaction fees.

summary: Prevents wallet fee-bumped transactions from receiving an `nLockTime` older than the transaction they replace. When `bumpfee` creates a replacement transaction, the original transaction's locktime is passed as a minimum bound to `DiscourageFeeSniping`, ensuring any random backdating stays between the original locktime and the active chain tip.
